question.text: An Equity-Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) has lock-in:

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) are equity-oriented mutual fund schemes that qualify for a tax deduction under Section 80C of the Income-tax Act (up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year under the old regime). To preserve the tax incentive, ELSS units are subject to a statutory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of allotment, the shortest among traditional 80C investment options. The Trap: "No lock-in" defeats the tax-incentive design; 5- and 10-year lock-ins describe other instruments (such as tax-saving FDs, NSC variants, or insurance products), not ELSS. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook supports the ELSS Section 80C tax deduction up to Rs. 1.5 lakh per financial year but does not explicitly state the 3-year lock-in on the pages checked. The 3-year lock-in is established by the ELSS scheme notification and Income-tax Rules and is presented here as general industry/regulatory knowledge.
